title: Contract revenue hides service burden
source_story: User-provided fictional owner stories in this conversation; opening narrative below is a faithful condensed adaptation, not a verbatim transcript.
owner_narrative: We know revenue and payroll but not service cost by account. Short remote calls look like long on-site repairs when both count as one ticket. Driving, repeat visits and van parts are missing. Renewal prices follow intuition.

diagnostic_interview.branch_if_answer_differs: High service cost may reflect an intentional strategic account or temporary project; profitability ranking alone does not dictate termination.

evidence.description: A simulated activity sample contains calls missing from tickets.
A simulated stock review finds unassigned part usage.
A simulated contract comparison mixes remote and multi-person work.

diagnoses.hypothesis: Inconsistent activity and cost attribution prevents meaningful contract-level economics.
diagnoses.counterhypothesis: High service cost may reflect an intentional strategic account or temporary project; profitability ranking alone does not dictate termination.
diagnoses.confidence_policy: Qualitative case-world support only; requires fresh customer evidence before reuse.

interventions.process_first: Collect lightweight activity categories and parts attribution; disclose completeness; agree direct cost and overhead conventions separately.
interventions.deterministic_and_assisted_automation: Aggregate attributable time and material cost; show ranges or unknowns for missing inputs and flag expensive repeat patterns.
interventions.rejected_default: Do not replace the whole service platform or deploy autonomous agents solely because the owner reports inefficiency.
interventions.selection_basis: Choose the least complex intervention addressing the supported handoff failure; compare added administration and integration burden.

requirements.statement: Do not equate ticket count with effort.
requirements.rationale: Inconsistent activity and cost attribution prevents meaningful contract-level economics.

requirements.statement: Do not label contribution margin as net profit.
requirements.rationale: Inconsistent activity and cost attribution prevents meaningful contract-level economics.

requirements.statement: Suppress precise margin when material cost inputs are missing.
requirements.rationale: Inconsistent activity and cost attribution prevents meaningful contract-level economics.

acceptance_tests.scenario_and_expected_result: A five-minute call and two-person visit receive different effort totals.
Missing rates result in unavailable cost, not zero cost.
Shared travel allocation reconciles to total travel.

capability_boundary.proposed_extension: Cost attribution and contract analytics are outside the existing six modules.
capability_boundary.pricing: No price assigned; current rate card must not be extended by analogy.

evaluation.primary_metric_definition: Percentage of service effort attributable to a contract; only then report contribution using disclosed cost conventions.
measurement_cautions: Use a stable denominator and comparable operating periods.
Record missingness and changed case mix.
Do not infer staff reductions from reclaimed task minutes.

implementation.baseline: Collect at least one representative operating cycle before rollout; for monthly billing or maintenance include the relevant full cycle. Extend sampling when volumes or seasonality make the sample unrepresentative.
implementation.scope: Start with one consenting customer group and the staff who own its handoffs; include a normal case and each listed exception.
sequence: Reconcile identities and existing obligations with the process owner.
Run the proposed rules in shadow mode; record disagreements and missed exceptions.
Approve a bounded live pilot only after requirements and exceptions have named owners.
Review outcome metrics, added administrative work and failure logs before expanding.
implementation.simulated_resolution: In this fictional case, MILO introduced the process change: Collect lightweight activity categories and parts attribution; disclose completeness; agree direct cost and overhead conventions separately. The team adopted the proposed workflow for the pilot scope. Routine coordination became explicit; unresolved exceptions continued to require a person.
implementation.simulated_lesson: High service cost may reflect an intentional strategic account or temporary project; profitability ranking alone does not dictate termination.
implementation.rollback: Pause automated writes and notifications, retain the event log, export outstanding work and return to a named manual coordinator. Reconcile queued events before resuming to avoid duplicate actions.
implementation.go_no_go: Process owner reviews coverage of acceptance cases, unresolved critical failures, metric direction and staff workload. No fixed performance threshold is claimed without customer agreement.

open_questions: Loaded labor rates, overhead policy and actual usage must be measured locally.

transfer_rules.applicable_when: Inconsistent activity and cost attribution prevents meaningful contract-level economics.
